text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Metro to become one big city: Al Leach to announce today Tories' plan to amalgamate six municipalities in Toronto region.
- Firms get first say on levels of toxics: Invited to modify pollution rules.
- Jean Chretien apologizes over GST promise: Liberals erred in '93 pledge, Prime Minister says.
- Panel opens door to private universities: Ontario should let post-secondary institutions set tuition, report urges.
- Mobutu returning home to nation in turmoil: Ailing Zairian dictator faces challenge of dealing with rebel insurgency, keeping election on schedule.
- Conrad Black selling Fairfax stake: Peeved press baron calls pledges to change Australian press ownership laws 'sandbag job.'
- Bre-X and Barrick submit Busang proposal: Firms say they 'can work together' to develop gold deposit.
- Magna sells airbag business: Deal for 80 percent stake in firms boosts cash hoard to $1.2 billion.
- Pay cut pays off for CIBC unit chief: Performance focus nets $4.9 million.
- Palliser dies as PanCanadian and Nova reach deal.

- Black pulls out of Fairfax: Hollinger sells 25 percent stake in Australian publisher for $513 million, fearing curbs on foreign owners might stay. Cash may be used to buy rest of Southam chain, says Black.
